## Proposed change

Add options flow to Hue (V2) integration which allows the user to specify devices for which they want to completely ignore the availability status. For example for misbehaving (non routing) 3rd party bulbs or just lights in a remote location having some connectivity issues.

I kept the logging in the code so users have some sort of clue about misbehaving devices and/or connectivity issues.

This will fix all the reported availability issues as the user has now all control how to treat unavailable devices.

issue_context.title: Hue bulbs not controllable via HASS while "unavailable" despite being controllable via hue
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The new API accurately shows the state of a hue bulb - however - apparently in hue "unavailable" doesn't mean "can't be turned on/off"

Several of my bulbs show as offline in my hue app at various times throughout the day, but they remain controllable via the hue app and, until recently, home assistant. 
Now HA sees these as unavailable and refuses to allow me to set them.
I don't have any idea how to troubleshoot this since this was never an issue before and, if I were using the hue app or Google home integration, still wouldn't be.
Please help

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.12.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2021.11.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

Hue

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
This means you have a routing issue in your Zigbee mesh.
Are the lights that are reported as unavailable official Hue lights ?
In that case it's just a signal strength issue. Try to move a light (or the bridge) to get better signal or place one or more lights in between the malfunction light to have wider range.

If its a 3rd party light that is just acting out all the time (shows as unavailable all the time in the Hue app), it means the light is not able to route at all. In that case the light will jump to available (and stay that way) the first time you control it.

HA doesn't allow controlling of unavailable devices/lights in the frontend, although direct service calls (e.g. automations, scripts) seem to allow it.

I hope you understand you actually have an issue in your setup/hardware and HA is kind enough to point you to it.
Ignoring it will result in bad/sluggish performance overall.

Hey there @balloob, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`hue`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L399) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

this is what I pointed at during the initial beta testing: before, Hue showed 'reachable: false' which made HA show 'unavailable' while in real life these lights (and other devices like motion sensors) even showed correct motion or other attributes, like daylight level. And where reachable with that. No clue why Hue api states that, or maybe it simply doesnt update frequently enough.
(the same is still happening btw for then led indicator, which are all 'off' on my api, but many sensors do show the light. The api simply isn't always correct.)

Also, even when a light cant be directly controlled, the group can be, and takes along the light, proving the point of the 'incorrectness' of the attribute reachable... even Google assistant manages at that moment.

Too bad HA can not guard this, or circumvent. Maybe even ignore that..

The HA frontend doesn't allow controlling unavailable entities. The direct service calls seem to accept it though.
The unavailable state is correct: It is attached to the "zigbee connectivity" of the device.

If a light is unavailable in the Hue app and HA it means that its 
**a)** powered off
or
**b)** having issues with connectivity, bad reception
or
**c)** not routing at all, such as most (all?) OSRAM lights if connected to a Hue zigbee mesh.

Both **b** and **c** can be killing for the performance/reliability of your entire setup, although it can be pretty safe to ignore case c if you have enough other lights available that route properly and those bad behaving lights can reach the bridge directly.
That situation will be auto detected by the HA integration and the availability check will be disabled.

If the API is not correct you should probably file an issue report with Signify ;-)
I think its 100% correct, at least the V2 api is from I've seen while working on this last couple of months. 
The V1 API has some quirks.

> The HA frontend doesn't allow controlling unavailable entities. The direct service calls seem to accept it though. The unavailable state is correct: It is attached to the "zigbee connectivity" of the device.

Okay... I'm talking to this via the hue hub though not ZigBee so...

> If a light is unavailable in the Hue app and HA it means that its **a)** powered off or **b)** having issues with connectivity, bad reception or **c)** not routing at all, such as most (all?) OSRAM lights if connected to a Hue zigbee mesh.

Again. Listed as unavailable in the hue app, but responds to the hue app. So not powered off. Its connectivity is good enough to respond. And these are first party hue devices. And as such, I don't control the routing.

> Both **b** and **c** can be killing for the performance/reliability of your entire setup, although it can be pretty safe to ignore case c if you have enough other lights available that route properly and those bad behaving lights can reach the bridge directly. That situation will be auto detected by the HA integration and the availability check will be disabled.

One of the lights that's doing this is a bulb that's remarkably close to the hub. It's in close proximity to three other bulbs that report fine. 

> If the API is not correct you should probably file an issue report with Signify ;-) I think its 100% correct, at least the V2 api is from I've seen while working on this last couple of months. The V1 API has some quirks.

I don't know what to tell you here. I can only describe the behavior I'm seeing.

As far as it being a "bug" with hue that I should file... Yeah that's great but the likelihood of them them fixing it is low since it's purely cosmetic on their end.

> This means you have a routing issue in your Zigbee mesh. Are the lights that are reported as unavailable official Hue lights ? In that case it's just a signal strength issue. Try to move a light (or the bridge) to get better signal or place one or more lights in between the malfunction light to have wider range. 

They are first party hue lights.
They are within two feet of other hue lights that never show an issue. They are within 20 feet of the hub.

> I hope you understand you actually have an issue in your setup/hardware and HA is kind enough to point you to it. Ignoring it will result in bad/sluggish performance overall.

What I understand is that everything works when I'm not using HA, and that your response appears to have a condescending tone that I do not appreciate. I hope I'm misreading that. 

From reading other responses here I see that I'm not the only person to have encountered this.

> Okay... I'm talking to this via the hue hub though not ZigBee so...

Your hub talks Zigbee to the lights.

If the Hue app lists them as unavailable and the Hue integration in Home Assistant does that too, then that is working correctly (data is 1-1 mapped).

Like Marcel said, your issue is with the Home Assistant frontend which does not allow interacting with unavailable devices. Home Assistant services do not include such checks.

@csanner what I'm trying to say is that it is not working correctly, as the Hue app also lists the lights as unavailable. While the Hue app allows ignoring that fact, Home Assistant doesn't. So my advice would be to track down why the light reports as unavailable. There's something wrong in the Zigbee mesh (Hue is based on that).

Ignoring it will lead to a bad experience with delays in commands and/or problems with adding more lights in the future.
So maybe you can just take one of those bad bulbs and move it to another location, just to check if that helps.
I am actually trying to help you here by telling to not ignore this alarm signal, not meant to be unhelpful.

> should probably file an issue report with Signify ;-)

Did also try their Facebook account which had more effect (we got the motion sensor switch back in the app ;-) ) 

Do you have other suggestions for doing that, filing an issue? Maybe if HA users join up there we can make more of an impression..

>  and that your response appears to have a condescending tone that I do not appreciate. I hope I'm misreading that.
>

...
wow, this is really making me feel ashamed. 
Next to being a huge asset for the HA community and the Hue integration, Marcel is one of the most helpful people around, always active and prepared to take the extra mile.

Even here, so: don't shoot the messenger! 
You mightn't like what you see, but HA is only showing us, not HA causing it. 

I usually dont try and interfere in these kind of personal comments (we should try to refrain from that completely I feel), but can not resist in this case. Please don't, all you do is publicly mirror your own mood. Not helpful.

Hue Integration in Ha has never been as robust and complete as it is now, so we all should thank Marcel for enabling us to enjoy Hue in HA like we currently can.

Merry Christmas!

I am experiencing this issue as well.  The bulbs I am having trouble with are outdoor spotlights, which are the farthest from my Hue bridge.  So @marcelveldt does make a very valid point regarding signal strength.  But they WERE working fine until the 2021.12 update, which seems very coincidental.

So first off, it sounds like I *was* misreading the tone. My apologies on that.
It probably comes from my frustration.

I know these lights are ZigBee, but I cannot use normal ZigBee methods to deal with them. And frankly my ZigBee lights and devices have never been as stable as my hue lights - up until now that is, but it's my hue experience that deteriorated, not my ZigBee that improved.

I appreciate the suggestions, though in my case the bulbs that go unavailable are not consistent, and frequently within inches of several other working bulbs (one out of three in a fixture) or in the same room as several others that are working fine, in relatively close proximity to the hub.
Meanwhile several of the lights farthest away, two floors down, have been rock solid.

I tried changing the ZigBee channel in the app a few times. Eventually I landed on one that seems sightly better than the others but now all my hue lutron dimmers say they're unavailable. Since I don't have those in HA maybe that's fine.

I understand that the HA experience is technically correct and the hue setup is technically at fault. I don't believe that's a great user experience though. If we can work with hue to fix this, great, but as a user that doesn't understand your integration code very well and whose setup is pretty much just working I foresee their response being "so everything we control seems to be working fine, have a nice day!"

I get your frustration. I've dealt with exactly the same issues. In the end it turned out to be some 3rd party light I added to my mesh, creating all kind of routing issues. Ditched that light from the setup and all issues were gone.
Also the location of the bridge and as you say, the zigbee channel can make a big difference.
Nevertheless it -might- be possible that you simply can't solve the issue with lights getting unavailable from time to time.

We map the data from the Hue API 1-on-1 to HA. there's one difference though. Hue will show a small mark that a light is reported unavailable but will still allow you to control it while HA simply blocks control that a light that is unavailable ( the frontend, the service calls do still work).

That makes you think if HA should do the same. Show a small warning sign or whatsoever on a light to inform you of the availability issue but still allow you to control it. Unlucky for us that is not possible as the unavailable status is mapped to the entity state and in the frontend the controls.

So, for the time being I came up with a (partly) intelligent solution to automatically ignore availability once we detect that a light is being controlled (outside the HA frontend) while being reported as unavailable. Once that happens, we simply ignore availability (and print a warning in the log).

That way users have a way to workaround it (by simply toggling the light in the Hue app or control the light (with an automation) through direct service call.

This workaround is not watertight: There's no way to tell the difference between a bad behaving light or a light that is simply without power. Back to the drawingboard...

At this moment I think the only solution left is to bring back a configuration option to ignore the availability state for lights, as discussed here:  https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/62807

I've been thinking about this for several days.
First off, thank you - this is *very* helpful information.
I have a much better idea of what's going on and why, as well as the technical challenges around dealing with it.

I'm still trying to think through the issue from a user standpoint, what would be best to see given the limitations described.

> I think the only solution left is to bring back a configuration option to ignore the availability state for lights

If this is a possibility, it gets my vote 100 times!  I suspected something changed in HA because I had zero noticeable Hue issues until the 2021.12 update. Glad to hear my suspicion was correct, and that there is a fix!

I do not use Hue any more (I am on Deconz). But I feel I have to help the users with the problem with some support. Philips Hue constantly report certain manufacturers devices unavailable. The users cannot do anything about it. It is a fact. The old integration had a setting to ignore unavailable. Without that set the Hue integration did not work at all. I had 7 devices that could never be controlled. All Osram. The minute I enabled the setting to ignore unavailable all worked as normal. You have to bring that option back if you want happy Hue users. It does not help the users to punish them for bugs made by Osram developers. And both Philips Hue and Osram/Lightify are big players on the smart lighting market. You cannot just ignore them.

The negative side that you cannot see when the mesh is broken is not very important for a normal user. It is more important that all your lights can be controlled from Home Assistant.
I think you've missed the whole conversation about a setting that will be added back to enable per-device support of ignoring availability.

> The negative side that you cannot see when the mesh is broken is not very important for a normal user. It is more important that all your lights can be controlled from Home Assistant.

Not true, if routing is not working properly on a mesh like zigbee, users will turn here for support when their lights are not responding properly etc. At least now we log that there might be something wrong.
